body:
WHAT
An addon is a Markdown procedure the agent can load on demand. Typing `/addons` prints every installed addon as a `/<name>` line with its description, then a second line naming the file it was loaded from (workspace-relative path, or the word `built-in`) and, when it is a directory addon, how many sibling files it bundles.

WHY
Without the file path a user who wants to edit or remove an addon has to guess which tier (built-in, home, workspace) it came from; without the bundle count they cannot tell a flat addon from one that ships scripts and notes.

WHERE
engine/core/src/runtime/engine.ts — Engine.handleSlash() case "addons" calls Engine.renderAddons(); the origin line uses relative(cwd, addon.path) or "built-in" and addon.resources.length; Engine.extensionLines() appends the installed count. Data comes from engine/core/src/agent/addons.ts — Addon.path / Addon.resources filled by loadAddons().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. With no addons loaded, `/addons` emits one command_output whose text starts with "No addons installed" and names .magentra/addons/ and ADDON.md.
2. With a workspace flat addon at .magentra/addons/foo.md, the output contains a line `/foo` followed by its description and a next line containing `(.magentra/addons/foo.md)` with no bundled-files suffix.
3. With a directory addon bar/ADDON.md plus two sibling files, the origin line reads `(.magentra/addons/bar/ADDON.md, 2 bundled file(s))`.
4. The built-in magentron addon is listed with origin `(built-in)` and never shows a bundled count.
5. The final line reports `Addons installed: N` where N equals the number of loaded addons.
